item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-10-16

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-16 00:40 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-16

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw is in a high-velocity release and hardening cycle. Over the last 24 hours the repo saw 500 issues updated (393 open/active, 107 closed) and 500 PRs updated (201 open, 299 merged/closed), plus 4 new releases spanning the 2026.10.10-beta.1 bleeding edge down to the 2026.9.33 extended-stable (LTS-equivalent) branch. The dominant engineering theme is Gateway performance and durability — the beta line is explicitly moving SQLite work off the main thread, while the issue tracker shows an ongoing cluster of WAL/checkpoint, plugin-capture, and update-reliability regressions. Overall project health is strong on throughput (a ~60% PR close rate in the window) but there is meaningful unresolved P0/P1 debt concentrated in storage-layer stability and plugin lifecycle.

2. Releases

Four releases shipped in the window:

🔷 v2026.10.10-beta.1 (Latest)

  • Highlights: Faster, steadier Gateway. Chat turns, session lists, startup, and idle Gateways do substantially less SQLite and main-thread work, with more database work moved onto worker threads so busy hosts and large agent fleets stay responsive. (#167965, #168002, #168093, …)
  • Breaking changes: None stated in release notes.
  • Migration notes: None stated; standard beta channel behavior applies.

🔷 v2026.10.5-beta.4

  • Highlights: More reliable updates — macOS updates no longer time out on aliased temporary directories; systemd user installs reclaim abandoned runtimes; pacman and FreeBSD installs defer to the package manager; snapshot failures are surfaced before applying.
  • Breaking changes: None stated.

🔷 v2026.10.4 (Stable)

  • Highlights: Gateway survives computer sleep and system clock jumps instead of restarting itself on a stale ownership heartbeat (#170790). Gateway shutdown/restart no longer hangs on certain paths. (Notes truncated in provided data.)
  • Breaking changes: None stated.

🟢 v2026.9.33 (extended-stable / LTS)

  • Gateway-only extended-stable release covering end-of-September 2026 OpenClaw plus critical security updates, reliability and performance fixes, and new model support. This is the branch recommended for operators who want stability over novelty.

Release takeaway: The beta train is churning fast (three beta/stable cuts in the window), which is consistent with the heavy Gateway refactoring underway in PRs like #173504 and #173523. Operators on LTS are being served with security backports rather than feature churn.

3. Project Progress

299 PRs merged/closed in the last 24h — a strong merge cadence. Notable active work visible in the top-of-queue PRs:

  • PR #173523 — refactor: simplify infra and plugin lifecycle bookkeeping (steipete). Removes redundant admission, producer-owned fact copying, and unsupported reentrant coordination from lifecycle paths. Flagged merge-risk: 🚨 availability, security-sensitive-changed.
  • PR #173504 — refactor(gateway): remove reload debt and startup claims. Cuts overlapping reservation/proxy-owner/restart-debt state in Gateway startup and config reload.
  • PR #173579 — fix: resume interrupted tasks in their original session. WebChat "Resume" now continues a saved task in the same session, preserving identity, workspace, participants, and children.
  • PR #173574 — perf(runtime): stop GC telemetry from waking idle workers (already closed). Directly aligned with the v2026.10.10-beta.1 "steady idle Gateway" theme.
  • PR #173548 — perf(subagents): release settled run text from memory (closed). Heap analysis identified ~25 MiB of retained task text across the registry — a memory-pressure fix.
  • PR #173266 — fix(control-ui): retain cached conversation titles on warm reload.
  • PR #173572 — fix(cron): ignore rate-limit cooldowns when Doctor records an automation account.

Advanced themes: Gateway lifecycle simplification, memory reclamation in subagents, Control UI Solid-migration perf cleanups, and CI infrastructure investment (Crabbox runner provisioning via #173581/#173582).

Notable closures: Issues #164113 (FICLONE EPERM in unprivileged LXC, P0), #121617 (post-compaction "Already compacted" misclassification, P0), #136262 (openai-completions stream text duplication, P1), and #170332 (beta update continuing after live DB change) all closed in the window.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment volume in the last 24h:

  1. Issue #143524 — 128 comments. Agent SQLite WAL grows to 1.4–2.8 GB in days despite wal_autocheckpoint=1000; blocks gateway startup (Windows, 2026.9.2/9.3). P0, impact:message-loss, impact:crash-loop. Despite the huge comment count, it remains open with clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr, indicating no fix PR is yet attached. Underlying need: durable WAL checkpointing under long-lived in-process readers — a recurring storage-architecture problem visible in two other issues below.

  2. Issue #160959 — 25 comments. Gateway blocks for minutes while capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression). P0, diamond-lobster rated. Need: plugin capture must be incremental/async and must not block the Gateway event loop.

  3. Issue #148707 — 20 comments. Reply lost with "Reply operation has no active tool authority snapshot" when a second run displaces an in-flight turn. P1, impact:session-state, impact:message-loss. Need: safe turn displacement / message-loss guarantees on session-state races.

  4. Issue #157989 — 18 comments. Plugin source capture rewrites ~1.1–1.4 GB per CLI command, ~6.5 GB per Gateway start; severe SSD wear. P1. Need: capture deduplication and reuse across invocations.

  5. Issue #68596 — 17 comments, 8 👍 (highest reaction). Feature Request: Configurable streaming watchdog timeout threshold. Need: users running long-reasoning models (kimi-k2.5, DeepSeek-R1) need to tune the 30s watchdog, which currently produces spurious "backend may have dropped this run" warnings.

  6. Issue #164294 — 17 comments. Gateway state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes (pinned by in-process reader). Need: same root-cause family as #143524 — an in-process reader is starving checkpoint progress. Directly relevant to the v2026.10.10-beta.1 "move DB work to worker threads" effort.

  7. PR #173523 and PR #173504 — top-of-queue PRs by review activity, both XL-scope Gateway refactors from the maintainer account (steipete), flagged for availability and security-boundary review.

Analysis: The comment-heavy issues cluster tightly around three root causes: (a) SQLite WAL/checkpoint lifecycle under concurrent readers, (b) plugin capture cost (CPU, I/O, SSD wear), and (c) message/session-state loss under turn races. These are exactly the areas the current beta line and Gateway refactors are targeting.

5. Bugs & Stability

P0 / Release-blocker severity (open):

Issue Impact Status
#143524 — WAL grows to 2.8 GB, blocks startup message-loss, crash-loop OPEN, no fix PR, 128 comments
#160959 — Gateway blocks minutes on plugin capture crash-loop OPEN, needs maintainer review
#70903 — file-based provider cooldown blocks users for hours after billing recovery auth-provider, UX release blocker OPEN (stale), no fix PR
#152275 — post-commit plugin activation failure leaves model catalog & reply dispatch dead until restart message-loss, crash-loop OPEN
#171918 — Safari 27.0.1 intermittently rejects Control UI entry graph UX release blocker OPEN, has synthetic repro
#161921 — after state-migrated-no-rollback, doctor --fix and plugins update deadlock each other UX release blocker OPEN

P1 severity (open):

  • #148707 — reply lost on displaced in-flight turn.
  • #157989 — plugin capture SSD wear.
  • #159512 — every subagent completion invalidates requester CLI session twice (claude-cli).
  • #164799 — agents admit slowly after version change; readyz returns 503 until restart.
  • #81182 — overflow recovery should truncate tool results before waiting the ~900s auto-compaction timeout.
  • #101793 — assistant text preceding a tool call silently dropped on Signal.
  • #77717 — Feishu channel bot identity recovery race → permanent disconnection.
  • #170956 — Windows slow startup, unclean plugin shutdown, schtasks permission errors.

Notable P2 stability items: #172091 (worker SQLite transaction pinned open forever, blocking shared-state checkpoints — filed 2026-10-14, directly adjacent to the beta Gateway work), #99659 (OOM kill after companion app connect), #81484 (Discord guild reply regression, repeated outbound loops), #166133 (MCP integer args coerced to string).

Closed in window (stability wins): #164113 (FICLONE EPERM in unprivileged LXC), #121617 (post-compaction guard misclassification), #136262 (openai-completions bare text_delta doubling message content), #170332 (beta update continued after live DB change), #77298 (cron consecutiveErrors inflated by restart interruptions).

Fix PR status: Most P0 issues carry clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr — i.e., no fix PR attached yet. The exceptions are #164113 and #121617, both now closed. The active Gateway refactor PRs (#173504, #173523) plausibly subsume several of the WAL/lifecycle fixes indirectly but are not explicitly linked as fixes.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

High-signal feature requests, grouped by likely roadmap proximity:

Likely to land soon (aligned with active PR/refactor work):

  • #79902 — companion-friendly SQLite transcript/session seams on top of the database-first runtime. The Control UI Solid migration and search-capability refactor (PR #172681) move in this direction.
  • #172091 / #164294 — WAL/checkpoint correctness. The v2026.10.10-beta.1 "worker-thread DB" thrust is the natural vehicle.
  • #81182 — truncate tool results before the full auto-compaction timeout. Low-risk, high-UX-value; memory-core is already an active PR target (#172681).

Plausible next-cycle candidates (clear scope, moderate effort):

  • #68596 (8 👍) — configurable streaming watchdog timeout. Strong user demand from reasoning-model users.
  • #67413 (5 👍) — per-agent dreaming configuration to prevent OOM during cron memory sweeps.
  • #67419 — stop re-injecting bootstrap files every turn (20–30% token waste). Pairs with the context-budget issues.
  • #71142 — configurable upload size limit for Control UI (currently hardcoded 5 MB).
  • #71452 — pagination for message list / channel-list instead of hardcoded 25-item truncation.

Longer-horizon / architectural:

  • #63990 — multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces).
  • #138245 — output guards to catch pseudo tool-calls emitted as plain text before they poison session history.
  • #66252 — per-agent TTS/STT overrides for multi-language deployments.
  • #103764 — Kotlin Multiplatform shared mobile logic.
  • #63930 — Anthropic advisor beta server-side tool support.

Prediction for next version: Given the v2026.10.10-beta.1 Gateway-perf direction, expect the next betas to include (a) further WAL/checkpoint fixes tied to worker-thread DB work, (b) plugin-capture reuse/dedup work, and (c) incremental Control UI Solid migration completions. The streaming-watchdog configurability request (#68596) has the clearest user-demand-to-effort ratio and is a strong candidate for inclusion.

7. User Feedback Summary

Satisfaction signals:

  • Users are actively stress-testing releases and filing detailed, high-quality repros (diamond- and lobster-rated issues), which reflects an engaged, technically sophisticated community.
  • Reactions skew positive on feature requests that propose configurability (8 👍 on #68596, 5 👍 on #67413), suggesting users trust the maintainers to respond to concrete, well-scoped asks.
  • The extended-stable / LTS line (#v2026.9.33) is a mature operational signal that the project is serving conservative production users, not just tinkerers.

Pain points (ranked):

  1. Storage-layer instability dominates. The three highest-comment issues (#143524, #164294, #172091) are all variants of the same root cause: SQLite WAL checkpoints starve behind long-lived readers. Users report multi-gigabyte WAL files, SSD wear, and Gateway startup failures — some have been open since September and are P0.
  2. Performance regressions from plugin capture (#160959, #157989) — minutes-long Gateway stalls and ~6.5 GB of I/O per Gateway start. Users on large plugin trees are materially blocked.
  3. Update reliability — macOS temp-dir timeouts, LXC seccomp/FICLONE failures, systemd abandonment, and state-migrated-no-rollback deadlocks. Multiple releases in the window are dedicated to this, indicating the maintainers hear the pain.
  4. Session/message loss races — displaced turns, dropped Signal text, subagent completion side-effects (#148707, #101793, #159512, #96975). Users perceive non-determinism in reply delivery, which is the worst class of bug for a personal-assistant product.
  5. Token/context economy — bootstrap re-injection (#67419), context-overflow over-counting (#101929), and Gemini textSignature bloat (#48709) all translate directly into user cost and latency.

Overall sentiment: Users are invested and precise, but the volume of P0/P1 storage and lifecycle bugs suggests production operators are being asked to absorb real risk. The rapid beta cadence and explicit LTS branch are correct mitigations, but closing the WAL cluster should be the top priority.

8. Backlog Watch

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — Personal AI Assistant / Agent OSS Ecosystem

Date: 2026-10-16
Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent open-source landscape is splitting into three tiers: OpenClaw at hyperscale, Hermes/QwenPaw/ZeroClaw in active productization, and IronClaw in a quiet eval-focused niche. Across the active projects, the dominant engineering pressure is the gateway/session layer: single-owner session state, durable storage, plugin lifecycle, multi-channel delivery, and provider routing. Security and observability are shifting from optional features to release gates, especially around plugins, MCP/approval flows, credentials, and multi-user identity. Contribution volume remains healthy in four projects, but merge/review throughput — not contributor interest — is the bottleneck outside OpenClaw.

3. OpenClaw’s Position

OpenClaw is the ecosystem’s scale leader by a wide margin: 500 issues and 500 PRs updated in 24h, with 299 PRs merged/closed and four releases including an extended-stable/LTS branch. Its peer activity is roughly 10x lower for Hermes, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw, and effectively dormant for IronClaw.

Advantages vs peers:

  • Largest community and maintainer throughput.
  • Mature LTS/stable/beta release structure.
  • Broadest operational surface: Gateway, Control UI, plugins, channels, cron, subagents, storage, updates.
  • Strong user sophistication: detailed P0/P1 repros, diamond/lobster-rated reports.

Technical approach differences:

  • Database-first runtime with explicit movement of SQLite work off the main thread onto worker threads.
  • Heavy Gateway lifecycle refactoring to remove reload debt and improve startup/idle behavior.
  • Plugin-capture and lifecycle bookkeeping being simplified, but still a major risk area.
  • LTS branch serves conservative operators; beta line carries aggressive Gateway hardening.

Key risk: The unresolved SQLite WAL/checkpoint cluster (#143524, #164294, #172091) is P0, months old, and has no linked fix PR. Plugin capture cost and update reliability are secondary but material. OpenClaw is the most mature project, but its storage-layer debt is the ecosystem’s largest single reliability risk.

Activity tiers:

  1. Hyper-scale / mature: OpenClaw — very high velocity, four releases, LTS, but significant P0 storage debt.
  2. Active productization / stabilizing: Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw.
    • Hermes: Post-unified-gateway fallout; corrective release; targeted fix PRs; trust issues from wrong-commit release.
    • QwenPaw: Stable v2.2.2; strong console/desktop work; but growing backlog and critical lifecycle/cancellation bugs.
    • ZeroClaw: Very high contribution volume, but 48 open PRs vs 2 closed; review-starved; no release in window.
  3. Low activity / niche: IronClaw — 1 issue, 0 PRs, 0 releases; benchmark-focused and quiet.

Rapidly iterating: OpenClaw, ZeroClaw, QwenPaw.
Stabilizing: Hermes, OpenClaw LTS branch.
Maturity ranking: OpenClaw > QwenPaw ≈ Hermes > ZeroClaw > IronClaw.

7. Trend Signals

  1. Gateway consolidation is the new architecture battleground. Projects are converging on a single gateway that owns sessions across CLI, desktop, bots, cron, and subagents. The hard problems are ownership, restart resilience, and avoiding silent cancellations.
  2. Storage work is moving off the main thread. OpenClaw’s beta explicitly moves SQLite to worker threads; peers show related durability and config-write concerns. Async storage is becoming a baseline expectation for responsive agent fleets.
  3. Plugin lifecycle is a security and reliability surface. OpenClaw, ZeroClaw, QwenPaw, and Hermes all have plugin/MCP/approval work in flight. Needs: deduplicated capture, hot reload, rollback safety, egress control, and supply-chain patching.
  4. Multi-channel reliability is table stakes. Email loops, WhatsApp voice-note drops, Signal text loss, Discord async result failures, and localisation fallbacks are recurring user-facing failures. Idempotency and delivery guarantees are now core product requirements.
  5. Observability is a UX feature, not just diagnostics. Users want tool receipts, partial output, progress streams, and cross-device visibility. Silent long-running turns are the most repeated UX complaint in ZeroClaw and QwenPaw.
  6. Provider routing and streaming correctness remain fragile. Stale base_url, forced non-streaming paths, OpenCode session headers, DSML parsing, and configurable watchdogs show that model/provider abstraction is still immature.
  7. Context/token economy is a direct cost and latency lever. Bootstrap re-injection, oversized tool results, base64 bloat, and output bounding are active concerns across OpenClaw, QwenPaw, and ZeroClaw.
  8. Identity, multi-user, and credential governance are rising. ZeroClaw’s OIDC/multi-user trackers, Hermes’ MCP/approval security, and OpenClaw’s security-sensitive PRs indicate enterprise/self-hosted deployments are pulling security forward.
  9. Platform parity matters. Windows startup, macOS LaunchAgent identity, Linux socket paths, and non-English locales appear as recurring friction. Cross-platform reliability is a maturity signal.
  10. Eval/model-quality taxonomies are emerging. IronClaw’s failure taxonomy shows a need for systematic benchmark diagnostics, especially where failures are model-quality rather than platform bugs.

  2. Critical — Hot reload cancels running cron tasks #8225 (open, 2.2.1). Saving a heartbeat setting via PUT /api/config/heartbeat aborts in-flight cron jobs, recorded as cancelled with no user notice. No fix PR.
  3. High — Hub restart drops desired-running runtimes; cron jobs silently skipped #8213 (open). Local process provisioner does not restore runtimes after restart; Hub can look healthy while schedules are missed.
  4. High — Doom-loop gate kills legitimate polling #8184 (open). Gate cannot distinguish "stuck repeating" from "waiting on a long-running background task," and cron subsequently records a false success.
  5. High — Frequent page load failure #8120 [CLOSED]. Reproduced on several devices; likely mitigated by #8260 (listen backlog 1 → 2048) and chunk-recovery fix.
  6. Medium-High — Plugin hot-install aborts on distro-patched Python 3.11 #8265 (open, 2.2.2). importlib.invalidate_caches() called unconditionally at loader.py:201/465/1094; raises on some builds and blocks installation.
  7. Medium-High — qwenpaw acp never loads plugins #8222 (open). PluginLoader is never instantiated in ACP sessions, so plugin tools and cross-process task callbacks are unavailable.
  8. Medium — qwenpaw-creator Windows failures: project deletion blocked by open creator.log (WinError 5, #8206) and startup abort on stale pid (SystemError not caught, #8194).
  9. Medium — Cron job editor corrupts values #8249 (2.2.2 beta5): default time resets to 00:00 and Request Content renders [object Object].
  10. Medium — Message-navigation directory mis-positions #8251 (2.2.2b4); follow-on to the #8186/#8214 navigation fixes.
  11. Medium — desktop.log never rotates on Windows #8185: sidecar tee handle defeats _SafeRotatingFileHandler.
  12. Low/Resolved — Model deprecation handling #8218 [CLOSED] (mimo-v2.5-free deprecated → mimo-v2.6-flash-free); provider session-header issues #7531/#7599 [CLOSED].

Pattern: cron/task-lifecycle cancellation bugs (#8252, #8225, #8213, #8184) form a coherent cluster and are the highest-value fix area; none currently has a linked fix PR.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

  • Cancellable skill-pool downloads with progress #8126 — directly follows merged work in #8055; likely to land soon given maintainer-initiated spin-off.
  • Firecrawl as a third web_search provider #8199 — implementation PR already open (#8200, first-time contributor, Under Review). High merge probability.
  • Tavily API key via credential store [#8174] → PR #8204 (Under Review).
  • Provider presets for CommandCode and Hugging Face Inference Providers #8233 — low effort, catalog expansion; plausible for a 2.2.x patch.
  • Delete action in Model Pool #8195 — purge deprecated models; pairs naturally with #8218.
  • Cross-device message visibility during in-flight runs #8202 — fix PR open (#8203).
  • i18n for protected execution contract prompt #8211 — extends the existing SCROLL_SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATES mechanism.
  • Optional host navigation policy #8223 — enterprise/curated deployment control, related to in-flight #8257.
  • Claude Code third-party harness #7396 — catalog entry still a placeholder in harnesses/registry.py.

Prediction for next release (2.2.3 / 2.3.0): Firecrawl + Tavily credential support, cross-device message echo, message-navigation fixes, plugin-catalog/installed-state fixes, and desktop startup/backlog fixes. Larger items (realtime voice, channels-as-plugins, PawApp SDK redesign, OpenUI) look targeted at a minor/major release rather than a patch.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points:

  • Desktop/web reliability and startup latency. #8120 (multi-device page load failures) and #8264 ("starts slowly, easily >10s before reaching the main interface; feels worse than workbuddy and Bean Bag") show the perceived experience gap versus competing assistants.
  • Task reliability under configuration changes. Users lose running cron jobs merely by saving settings (#8225) or restarting the Hub (#8213), and the failures are silent.
  • Multi-agent orchestration fragility. The #8252 fleet user is running an Orchestrator/Reasoner/Executor/Reviewer/Defender topology with a Feishu channel gateway — a sophisticated production use case whose sessions are being cancelled without diagnostics.
  • Windows as a second-class platform. #8185, #8194, #8206 all cluster on Windows (log rotation, stale pid, file locks).
  • Provider drift. OpenCode header/session requirements (#7531, #7599) and model deprecations (#8218) break working setups without user action.

Satisfaction signals: Positive reception of 2.2.x console investments (themes, in-Chat terminal) and enthusiasm for the third-party harness feature (Codex and Qoder supported; Claude Code eagerly awaited in #7396). First-time contributors are actively submitting PRs (#8012, #8200, #8204, #8259) — a healthy community funnel. Dissatisfaction concentrates on reliability and perceived latency rather than missing features.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-standing or high-importance items lacking recent resolution:

  • #7396 — Claude Code as a third-party agent harness — status and roadmap? Open since 2026-08-28; two comments, no maintainer roadmap answer. Users can see the placeholder in source, so silence is a visible gap.
  • #7565 — clean plugin unload and rollback-safe hot reload (opened 2026-09-04, size/XXXL). Directly relevant to today's plugin hot-install failure (#8265) and hot-reload cancellation (#8225); needs review bandwidth.
  • #7785 — realtime voice chat (opened 2026-09-15, size/XXXL). Long-running feature PR without visible merge signal.
  • #7874 — redesign the PawApp SDK and app control plane (opened 2026-09-19, size/XXXL). Note #8266 explicitly ships Data App 1.0.3 independently of Host vNext, implying this redesign is still far from landing — worth a public status note.
  • #7903 — integrate QwenPaw community and inbox (opened 2026-09-20, size/XXXL, [wip]).
  • #8012 — Telegram fenced-code rendering fix from a first-time contributor (opened 2026-09-29); small, user-visible, and a good candidate for prompt review to retain the contributor.

Recommendation: Prioritize a maintainer response on #7396 (roadmap clarity) and a review pass on #7565, since plugin lifecycle correctness underpins three of today's open bugs.

ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw

ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-10-16

1. Today's Overview

ZeroClaw remains in a high-churn, pre-release development phase: 27 issues and 50 pull requests were updated in the last 24 hours, yet no new releases landed and zero issues were closed, with only two PRs closed (one a superseded Dependabot bump, one a security patch). The open PR queue has grown to 48 items, several of them size:XL / risk:high and tagged for release:v0.8.6 or release:v0.9.0, indicating a large review backlog relative to merge throughput. Bug activity skews heavily toward the email and WhatsApp channel implementations, with a cluster of S2 (degraded behavior) reports filed by the same contributor in a single day. Strategic work continues around the WASM plugin system, runtime/gateway separation, and the OIDC/multi-user security milestones, all of which remain tracked as open milestones rather than shipped. Overall health: very active, but merge- and release-starved — the project is accumulating validated work faster than maintainers are closing it.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours. No release notes, breaking changes, or migration guidance to report.

3. Project Progress

Only two PRs left the open queue today:

  • #11755 [CLOSED] — fix(deps): patch Wasmtime and Rustls security advisories. Bumped the locked Wasmtime family 48.0.5 → 48.0.6 (plus Pulley/Cranelift alignment) and raised three direct plugin dependency minimums to 48.0.6, addressing 14 Wasmtime RustSec findings. This is the most concrete stability win of the day. (PR #11755)
  • #11723 [CLOSED] — Dependabot rust-all group bump (30 updates), closed as superseded by #11776 (same group with 31 updates). (PR #11723, PR #11776)

Feature work advanced in-review but not merged, notably the plugin lifecycle stack from IftekharUddin (#11236 recovery of incomplete installs, #11261 staged admission replacement, #11262 verified zeroclaw plugin update, #11309 quickstart plugin install, #11347 shipping the WASM plugin host in release artifacts, #11311 artifact smoke harness, #11304 egress-denial logging). Per the OIDC tracker (#8289), the core OIDC stack and the consolidated enrollment/gateway/private-memory slices (#11082) have previously landed, leaving that effort in close-out.

4. Community Hot Topics

Ranked by comment count in the last 24h window:

Item Comments Theme
#7952 8 Release-shape confusion — optional channels-full prebuilt bundle vs. lean default
#7432 7 Tracker for runtime Phase 2 (v0.8.6) and gateway separation (v0.9.0)
#10531 6 Delegate sub-agent progress visibility (tool receipts, partial output)
#8763 4 ZeroCode UI for subagent activity and expandable tool results
#8289 4 OIDC canonical principals / inbound authentication tracker
#10426 3 User-facing agent progress in Telegram

Underlying needs analysis: The comment leaders cluster around two distinct anxieties. First, operator confidence — users cannot see what delegated sub-agents are doing (#10531, #8763, #10426), and the release packaging debate (#7952) reflects friction when a configured channel doesn't work with the shipped binary. Second, architectural durability — the runtime/gateway (#7432) and OIDC (#8289) trackers are long-lived sources of truth, suggesting contributors want contract stability before building further on these surfaces.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by reported severity:

S1 — Workflow blocked

  • #11130 — DeepSeek DSML tool-call markup is not parsed; raw markup leaks to the channel and the turn ends silently. Root cause is in the shared tool-call parser, with symptoms in channel and runtime. status:in-progress, so a fix is believed underway. (related #11742 broadens this to custom OpenAI-compatible providers defaulting to text-fallback.)

S2 — Degraded behavior

  • #10114 (p1) — max_tool_result_chars is a fixed 50,000 default, unrelated to the model's actual context window.
  • #10116 (p1, follow-up) — Oversized tool results are cut byte-wise middle-out; should spill to a file handle as web_fetch does.
  • #11745 — Email channel does not store inbound attachments as documented.
  • #11749 — Email channel answers auto-replies, bounces, and list mail, risking mail loops.
  • #11760 — Email channel re-answers live mail after every restart (active mode never sets \Seen).
  • #11761 — Email channel misses mail arriving during a fetch until the next IDLE timeout (default 29 min).
  • #11764 — WhatsApp Web silently drops untranscribed voice notes.
  • #11773 — Regional OS locales (fr_FR, es_ES, ja_JP) fall back to English.
  • #11771 — Bootstrap file cap mismatch: 20,000 chars on gateway turns vs. 6,000 (with compact_context) on channel/agent-loop turns.

S3 — Minor

  • #11769 — Four channel tests hard-code English notice text and fail under other locales.
  • #11758 — WhatsApp Web keeps printing pairing QR codes for ~2.5 min after its listener stops.

Fix PRs present? Partially. #11297 restores keep_tool_context_turns semantics, #10391 tightens bounded-delegate workspace/tool/command policy, #11672 fixes JPEG admission projection, and the Wasmtime/Rustls advisories were patched (#11755). No fix PR is visible for the email-cluster or WhatsApp-cluster bugs (#11745, #11749, #11760, #11761, #11764, #11758), which is the most concerning stability gap today.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Concrete feature requests updated today, mapped to release tags where present:

  • Release/packaging: #7952 — optional broad-channel prebuilts (channels-full).
  • Agent observability: #10531, #8763, #10426, #11743 — progress/thinking streams for delegate, ZeroCode, Telegram, and Slack.
  • RFC: #11735 — bounded tool and delegate results at the turn boundary (directly addresses the same pain as #10114/#10116).
  • Email channel hardening: #11747 (SMTP STARTTLS / Office 365:587), #11751 (tls_ca_cert_path for private CAs).
  • Config/UX: #10665 (configurable ZeroCode per-pane session limit), #11753 (configurable ack reaction emoji).

Prediction for the next version (v0.8.6, then v0.9.0): the strongest near-term signal is the WASM plugin lifecycle — a half-dozen stacked, release:v0.8.6-tagged PRs (#11236, #11261, #11262, #11309, #11347, #11311) plus the already-landed security patch (#11755). Also likely to ride along: the eleven-built-in-tools default (#11221) and the runtime delivery items in the #7432 tracker. OIDC (#8289) and multi-user isolation (#8290) are explicitly release:v0.9.0 and remain close-out trackers rather than fresh work. The turn-boundary bounding RFC (#11735), if accepted, may be picked up in a v0.9.x cycle.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points voiced by real users:

  • Silent long-running turns. Operators on Telegram (#10426) and delegating agents generally (#10531) describe requests that "look stalled" because no intermediate progress is surfaced. This is the single most repeated UX complaint across issues.
  • Email channel is not production-trustworthy. A single contributor (RustLangLatam) filed five email issues in two days covering attachments, auto-reply loops, \Seen state after restart, IDLE-timeout mail loss, STARTTLS, and private-CA trust. This reads as an operator attempting a real mailbox deployment and hitting a wall.
  • Configuration surprises. #7952 (channels not in the lean prebuilt) and #11742 (custom provider silently defaulting to text-fallback) both reflect confusion when defaults don't match documented expectations. #11771 (differing bootstrap caps by turn path) is the same class of "the config says one thing, the runtime does another."
  • Localization treated as second-class. #11773 and #11769 show non-English locales (fr_FR, es_ES, ja_JP) degrading to English or breaking tests.

Satisfaction signals: contributors are engaged and producing detailed, well-scoped bug reports with file/line references; the security patch and active p1 in-progress items show responsiveness on high-severity paths. Dissatisfaction concentrates on channel reliability and visibility — the areas with the least PR coverage in today's data.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived or high-importance items needing maintainer attention:

  • #7952 — open since 2026-06-19, 8 comments, tagged status:icebox despite status:accepted and risk:high. Highest-comment issue in the window with no visible movement.
  • #7432 — open since 2026-06-09, the v0.8.6/v0.9.0 runtime/gateway tracker; effectively gates the next two releases.
  • #8289 and #8290 — both open since 2026-06-24, topic:identity-access, risk:high, marked as close-out trackers for v0.9.0. They need explicit sign-off or closure to unblock downstream planning.
  • PR #10430 — Gemini speech-to-speech channel, open since 2026-08-28, needs-author-action, status:parking-lot, size:XL.
  • PR #10391 — bounded-delegate policy enforcement, open since 2026-08-26, needs-author-action; directly relevant to the delegate-boundary RFC (#11735).
  • PR #10499 — persistent config write validation, open since 2026-08-31, needs-author-action, risk:high.
  • PR #11221 — eleven-built-in-tools default, open since 2026-09-29, needs-author-action, release:v0.8.6 and release:v0.9.0; a release-gating change with no merge despite active rebasing.
  • PR #11304 — plugin egress-denial logging, explicitly status:blocked.
  • #11130 — S1 DSML parser bug, status:in-progress with no linked PR visible; warrants a status check given its workflow-blocking severity.

Bottom line: the project's bottleneck is review throughput, not contribution volume. With 48 open PRs against 2 closures and a release-gating item (#11221) aging in needs-author-action, the healthiest next step would be triaging the v0.8.6 plugin stack and the unaddressed email/WhatsApp bug cluster.

item.content:encoded:
AI 基础设施日报 2026-10-16

生成时间: 2026-10-16 00:40 UTC | 覆盖项目: 6 个

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

横向对比

跨项目 AI 基础设施对比 — 2026-10-16

1. 生态系统概览

AI 基础设施活动仍然极度活跃，但重心已从原始吞吐量转向正确性、缓存安全性和智能体/工具可靠性。服务引擎正竞相在 GB300、Blackwell SM120、ROCm/MI355X 和 Apple/消费级硬件上支持 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash、GLM-5.3、Qwen3.x、Kimi K3、Muse Spark Open 和 Nemotron 3.5。与此同时，多个高严重度问题都是静默正确性 bug——PD 分离中的陈旧 KV、前缀缓存跨请求污染、工具定义被剥离，以及网关预算/支出绕过。稳定版发布有限：llama.cpp 发布 v0.7.0，Unsloth 发布 beta，LiteLLM 发布预发布版，而 vLLM/SGLang/Ollama 在此窗口无新版本。

2. 活跃度对比

N/R = 摘要未披露 24 小时总数。在可获得时，数量按“过去 24 小时内更新”统计。

项目 过去 24 小时更新的 Issue 过去 24 小时更新的 PR 发布状态
vLLM 121 500 无新版本；无正式破坏性变更
SGLang N/R N/R 无新版本；正在移除 Python 3.10；无 API 移除
llama.cpp 47 149 v0.7.0 / b11669；b11671 Muse Spark Open；b11658 maion-coder；b11662；b11643；b11642
Ollama N/R N/R 过去 24 小时无版本发布
LiteLLM N/R N/R v1.107.0-dev.2、v1.106.0-rc.4 预发布版；cosign Docker 验证
Unsloth N/R N/R v0.1.908-beta

解读： vLLM 和 llama.cpp 披露的原始更新量最大。vLLM 以 PR 为主且聚焦正确性；llama.cpp 正在交付发布内容。SGLang 主要由 CI/稳定性和 SM120/GLM-5.3 问题占据。Ollama、LiteLLM 和 Unsloth 的活动分别集中在智能体/工具正确性、网关可运维性以及训练/模型接入上。

3. 模型支持竞赛

已发布/已落地支持：

  • llama.cpp： v0.7.0 新增 GLM5-Next MTP、K2 Horizon dense/MoVA、Prism 以及主机内存 MoE 专家缓存。b11671 新增 Muse Spark Open 文本/视觉/音频。b11658 新增 maion-coder 以及 draft-model 支持。
  • Unsloth： v0.1.908-beta 新增 NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 / Bolt（24 GB）、Meta Muse Spark Open、文本扩散 LLM、DeepSpeed 训练，并改进了面向编码智能体的提示缓存。FLUX.3 Image Klein 加载已在 PR 中。
  • Ollama： 通过升级 llama.cpp 修复 MiniCPM-V 4.7 projector 支持；新增 Q2_0 GGUF 支持；新增 Clippy Vision 和 Clef Cloud。
  • LiteLLM： 不是模型内核项目，但在提供方兼容性上有所推进，包括 Bedrock Claude Web 身份、OpenAI gpt-transcribe、Anthropic compaction blocks、Bedrock Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 token 计数、Kimi K3 / DeepSeek framing，以及 Databricks gpt-5.6 工具/推理问题。

进行中/尚未发布：

  • vLLM： Muse Spark Open、ROCm 上的 Step-5-Preview、DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GB300 低延迟解码、ROCm fused QK-norm + RoPE + gate kernels。Nemotron 3.5 ASR 流式、Phi4Flash 和 ViT full CUDA graph 属于请求/RFC。
  • SGLang： DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 的 SM120 现场报告；GLM-5.3-Flash SM120 跟踪；Hopper CuTe DSL KDA verify kernel；AMD AITER/DSv4 GEMM 工作；Muse Spark Open NIXL KV packing。

谁领先？

  • 已发布的本地模型支持广度： llama.cpp 和 Unsloth 领先。
  • 新加速器上的数据中心服务支持： vLLM 和 SGLang 领先，尤其是在 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash、GLM-5.3、ROCm/MI355X 和 GB300/SM120 方面。
  • 提供方/API 兼容性： LiteLLM 领先。
  • 智能体正确性： 由于原生 /api/chat 工具定义问题，Ollama 目前落后。

4. 性能前沿

优化工作集中在五个方面：

KV 缓存与前缀缓存

  • vLLM：PD 分离前缀缓存污染、KV connector 缓存有效性、模型定制 KVCache 规划、Mamba block-size 回归。
  • SGLang：HiCache 陈旧 KV 静默损坏、统一内存池预热/压缩、NIXL KV packing。
  • llama.cpp：提示缓存现在仅保存可恢复的 slot 状态；--moe-cache-mib 主机专家缓存。
  • Unsloth：用于并发聊天的 KV 抢占、面向编码智能体的提示缓存。

批处理与解码延迟

  • vLLM：DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GB300 低延迟解码、DSpark 投机解码、FA2 短查询/长上下文注意力。
  • SGLang：面向 EAGLE 低并发解码的 AMD FP8 quant+GEMM 融合、PP-spec 比较跳过。
  • Ollama：MLX 引擎仍为单请求串行；无连续批处理。
  • Unsloth：通过 llama-server KV parking/preemption 实现并行聊天服务。

量化与低位格式

  • llama.cpp：Q1_0/Q2_0 numpy 支持、Hexagon Q1_0 提案、重新打包重构。
  • Ollama：Q2_0 GGUF 张量/文件类型支持。
  • Unsloth：compile 下的 4-bit MoE 反量化、FLUX.3 INT8/FP8/GGUF。
  • vLLM/SGLang：NVFP4 OOM、W4A16 路由专家、FP8 KV。

分布式服务

  • vLLM：TP4 + DSpark、PD 分离、MoE 精确步长、混合 GDN 前缀缓存命中。
  • SGLang：NIXL TP 异构传输、PD prefill + HiCache、DCP planner 崩溃。
  • llama.cpp：MTP 多 GPU 提示处理回归；Vulkan 多设备 + CPU-MoE 变慢。
  • LiteLLM：网关负载测试、重试/退避、WebSocket 支出核算、Rust 路由对齐。

内核

  • vLLM：FA2 优化、ROCm Triton 融合内核、Mamba2 NaN 修复。
  • SGLang：AMD FP8 GEMM 融合、Hopper 上的 CuTe DSL KDA verify、deepstack CUDA-graph 处理。
  • llama.cpp：Metal BF16 tensor-API flash attention、Vulkan f16 KV striding、Hexagon 张量重新打包。
  • Unsloth：ROCm flash attention 计时探测、torch.compile 外的 MoE 反量化、混代 GPU 能力检测。

5. 层级定位

层级 项目 主要关注点 今日信号
服务引擎 vLLM, SGLang 高吞吐分布式 GPU 推理、分页注意力、PD 分离、投机解码 前缀缓存/PD 中的正确性 bug 是最大风险；新硬件支持活跃
本地运行时 llama.cpp, Ollama 单节点/桌面/边缘推理、GGUF、广泛硬件 llama.cpp 正在交付 MoE offload/spec decode；Ollama 在智能体/工具调用正确性上挣扎
网关 LiteLLM 多提供方路由、认证、预算、支出日志、重试、MCP 预算绕过、支出表膨胀、RAM/OOM 和 /v1/messages 兼容性是关键风险
训练/微调 Unsloth LoRA/RL/GRPO、模型接入、Studio UI、AMD/NVIDIA 支持 对 Nemotron 3.5/Muse Spark 的 beta 支持；多 GPU 微调仍在路线图，沙箱不够严密

重叠： Ollama 底层依赖 llama.cpp/MLX。Unsloth 也涉及推理/Studio 服务。vLLM 和 SGLang 越来越多地用于 RL rollout 和智能体后端，这使它们暴露在训练循环正确性要求之下。

6. 趋势信号

  1. 静默正确性如今是主导性的基础设施风险。
    vLLM 的 PD 前缀缓存串扰、SGLang 的 HiCache 陈旧 KV bug、Ollama 的工具定义被剥离，以及 LiteLLM 的预算/支出绕过，都会在没有明确错误的情况下失败。智能体开发者应添加输出金丝雀、禁用有风险的前缀缓存，并监控支出表。

  2. 新模型支持速度在本地运行时和训练栈中最高。
    llama.cpp 和 Unsloth 已发布 Muse Spark Open、Nemotron 3.5、GLM5-Next、K2 Horizon 和文本扩散支持。vLLM/SGLang 仍在为新加速器启用 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash、GLM-5.3 和 Qwen3.x。

  3. 硬件多样化正在加速——硬件特定回归也在加速。
    GB300、Blackwell SM120、ROCm MI355X、Strix Halo、Vulkan、Metal、Hexagon 和 MIG 均出现。SM120 明确是“最少经过实战检验”的；在修复前的构建上，不应信任多 GPU 异构和 MIG 决策。

  4. 投机解码和 MoE offload 是主要性能杠杆——但也伴随回归。
    vLLM DSpark、llama.cpp LiliCorr/MTP、SGLang EAGLE/DSPARK 和 MoE 主机缓存带来大幅收益，但 MTP 多 GPU 提示处理和 Vulkan MTP 断言是当前活跃的回归。

  5. 网关运营化正在成熟。
    LiteLLM 正在增加重试/退避、WebSocket 支出核算、负载测试套件、CLI 冷启动改进和 Rust 路由对齐。对于生产环境，成本/预算正确性和 /v1/messages 稳定性仍是关注项。

  6. 智能体工作负载正在给每一层带来压力。
    工具 schema 校验开销、流式解析器 chunk 边界 bug、GLM-5.3-Flash 退化、沙箱逃逸风险和空工具定义均存在。工具调用应优先使用 /v1 而非 Ollama 原生 /api/chat；在 vLLM 中校验 strict/required/named 工具选择；并将 Unsloth 沙箱视为尚不是安全边界。

  7. 本周期中，锁定版本比往常更重要。
    SGLang 正在为 CUDA 构建移除 Python 3.10；Unsloth 正在以 transformers 5.20.0 和 TRL < 0.28 为基准重新调整；LiteLLM 预发布版仅支持 cosign；llama.cpp 的 v0.7.0 改变了提示缓存和 MTP 行为。在 CI 和生产环境中有意识地冻结版本。

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM 摘要 — 2026-10-16

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有新的 vLLM 版本发布，但开发活动仍然活跃。当前最值得关注的进行中工作包括面向 GB300 的 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 低延迟解码栈（#61868, #61869）、ROCm Step-5-Preview 支持（#61837），以及面向短查询/长上下文工作负载的 FA2 注意力优化（#61784）。最严重的未解决正确性问题是启用自动前缀缓存的 PD 分离场景中的跨请求上下文污染（#61160）；相关的 KV 连接器缓存有效性 bug 也仍处于打开状态（#61768）。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序。

  • 严重 — 跨请求 KV 污染：在 NIXL prefill/decode 分离中启用自动前缀缓存时，响应可能间歇性包含其他请求的内容；可通过 --no-enable-prefix-caching 规避（#61160）。仍打开，本数据中无修复 PR。
  • 严重 — 静默 CUDA IMA：在 RTX 3090 上，hybrid GDN + MTP k=3 + 异步调度可能在非法内存访问后以退出码 0 退出；此前的修复均未解决（#53726）。仍打开。

  • 中高 — Blackwell OOM：在 16 GB Blackwell 上使用 NVFP4 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 时，在 profile_run 内部分配的 FlashInfer b12x SM120 MoE 工作区会 OOM（#49476）。仍打开。
  • 中 — Mamba 配置回归：移除 mamba_cache_mode="all" 后，--mamba-block-size 不再生效（#60838）。仍打开。
  • 中 — ROCm P/D 挂起：在 AMD GPU P/D 运行中，MoRI/MoRIIO READ 模式 KV 传输可能挂起或仅部分完成（#45749）。仍打开，已陈旧。

  • LoRA/RL RFC：跟踪 RL rollout 中未解决的 LoRA 正确性与生命周期问题（#48297）。仍打开。
  • 已修复/已关闭：/v1/embeddings 在输入被截断时死锁（#55427）；ROCm Kimi K2.5 MXFP4 decode ITL 回归（#45943）；重复的 hash-routing 方法导致 mypy 失败（#61924）；DP=1 的 TP 分片 routed-expert 捕获（#61388）。

SGLang — sgl-project/sglang

SGLang 摘要 — 2026-10-16

1. 今日要点

CI 稳定性工作占据今日关注焦点：flaky-test 跟踪器 #42752（83 条评论）以及现已关闭的 CI 维护模式 issue #21065，反映出 PR Test Base/Extra 运行仍在持续波动。在 serving 侧，当天最严重的信号是 PD prefill + HiCache 中的一个静默正确性缺陷（#44070），其中 decode 可能收到陈旧 KV；同时还出现一批 SM120 / GLM-5.3-Flash 报告。性能工作覆盖 AMD FP8 GEMM 融合、NIXL TP 异构传输，以及对 CuTe DSL KDA verify 内核的 Hopper 支持。

2. 发布与破坏性变更

过去 24 小时无新版本发布。

  • 正在进行 Python 3.10 移除 — #44393 将剩余的 CUDA sglang-kernel wheel 路径（cp310-abi3）及相关 CI/发布任务迁移到 Python ≥3.11，接续 #43021。非 CUDA 硬件路径明确不在本 PR 范围内。任何为 CUDA 构建固定 3.10 运行时的用户都应计划升级。
  • 今日未宣布 API/配置移除；用于可选启用 toktier tokenizer 后端的 RFC（#44374）仅处于提案阶段。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • SM120（RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell，仅 PCIe） — 关于 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 在 8× RTX PRO 6000 上的现场报告，包含实测 prefill/decode 以及投机解码 A/B（#40877）。另一个跟踪 issue 覆盖 GLM-5.3-Flash 在 SM120 TP2 上所需的修复，涉及 W4A16 路由专家、FP8 KV、视觉和原生 MTP（#37813）。
  • Hopper（SM90）KDA verify 内核 — #44612 将融合的 CuTe DSL KDA（fused_kda_decode_mtp_dspark）verify 内核扩展到 SM90；此前因成对 FP32 指令仅限 SM100+。
  • AMD / ROCm — AITER 升级就绪跟踪器仍活跃（#21302）；PR #44008 携带调优后的 DSv4 GEMM 行和 mHC tile_m=16，直到上游 AITER 发布这些内容。扩散多模态单元测试正在改为 ROCm 感知（#44599）。
  • Tokenizer 后端 RFC — toktier，一个可选启用的精确增量式与 chunk 并行 CPU tokenizer 后端（#44374）。
  • Monokernel 框架 RFC — 树内 python/sglang/experimental/monokernels/ 插件模型，用于逐模型融合内核（#43949）。

4. 性能与优化

  • AMD MI355X，Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8：将 1x128 激活量化（约 4 µs）融合进 small-M block-scale GEMM（约 9 µs），按每个 dense FP8 projection 计 — 面向 EAGLE 低并发 decode（#42229）。
  • AMD linear-attn：在 Qwen3.5-397B 的 GDN/KDA verify 路径上跳过未使用的 PP-spec 比较（#43861）。
  • 用于 TP 异构传输的 NIXL KV packing（Muse Spark Open）（#44615）。
  • 统一内存池：启动时预热 compaction move，并按 page id 复制整页 page envelope，从而从服务路径中移除首次使用时的内核编译/加载和 _assert_async 开销（#44592）。
  • Diffusion 运行时导入：在约 10k 模块导入期间推迟完整 GC 回收，避免重复的完整堆追踪（#44606）。
  • 工具 schema 校验：用 jsonschema-rs 替换纯 Python 的 Draft202012Validator.check_schema（约 0.7 ms/工具；在 API 事件循环上，一个 18 工具 agent 请求约 12 ms）（#43274）。
  • CUDA graph：让 deepstack media prefill 保持 eager，这样 Qwen3-VL 系列的 graph replay 不会复用陈旧的 input_deepstack_embeds（#44607）。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序；有修复 PR 的已注明。

  1. 静默 KV 损坏 — PD prefill + HiCache（#44070）：在默认 SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_EARLY_SEND_CACHED_PREFIX=1 下，当两个请求共享一个其 KV 仅存在于主机内存中的前缀时，decode 可能对部分前缀收到陈旧 KV。会静默产生错误结果，而不是崩溃。未引用修复 PR。
  2. 客户端断开导致整引擎崩溃（#39216）：未捕获的 asyncio.CancelledError 绕过 except Exception；在 4× RTX 6000D / DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 上可复现。
  3. 整个 TP 组 OOM 崩溃（#41076）：DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSPARK 下 SparsePrefillWorkspace 无界分配。
  4. Kimi K3 decode 崩溃（#34920）：PD disagg + --dcp-size 8 + DSPARK target-verify 在 dcp/planner.py 中触发 cumsum(extend_prefix_lens=None)；所有 TP rank 均挂掉。
  5. GLM-5.3-Flash 在 DFLASH 投机解码下输出退化（#40843）：推理输出中出现严重重复/循环。
  6. GLM-5.3-Flash 在 agentic 提示下出现 ! 循环（#36669）：复杂 system prompt + 多个工具 + tool_choice=auto 会使 thinking 输出退化。
  7. SM120 attention 后端矩阵（#42012）：fa4 在 hybrid extend reshape 的 CUDA-graph capture 时崩溃；在测试过的 v0.5.20 镜像上，triton 是唯一可用的后端。
  8. NIXL PD abort 挂起（#44369）：abort 可能让所有默认传输 worker 一直等待健康的非终止 handle。
  9. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 静默语义损坏（#37111）：GB10 TP2 上的 QSA + NEXTN decode graph。
  10. 同步请求预处理阻塞事件循环（#30770），导致 health endpoint 延迟 — 仅 CPU 的确定性复现。
  11. 无界多模态音频解码（#43708）。
  12. 次要/测试基础设施：WeightChecker.reset_tensors 用随机值填充 MRotaryEmbedding.axis_map（#44501）；profiler 文件名路径穿越，经由调用方控制的 output_dir/profile_prefix（#44609，修复 PR 开放中）。
  13. CI 抖动：跟踪器 #42752；NIXL 存储测试共享固定的 /tmp 目录（#44613，修复 PR 开放中）；hicache prefetch 超时预算在每次重试时重新发放（#44614，修复 PR 开放中）。

今日关闭：#34340（SM103 被误门控为 SM100 系列，cutedsl TGV BF16 GEMM / trtllm-gen MoE finalize）、#36333（来自断开流式客户端的僵尸请求）、#21065（CI 维护模式）、#23494（AMD Q2 路线图，标记为不活跃）、#41303（DeepSeek-V4.1 SWA 有界重放窗口）、#44599（ROCm 感知 diffusion 测试）。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 仔细验证 PD + 前缀缓存。 如果你在 HiCache 下运行 disaggregated prefill，并带有共享 system prompt（常见的 agent 场景），#44070 意味着相同前缀可能产生细微错误的输出，且不会暴露任何错误。在修复前可考虑设置 SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_EARLY_SEND_CACHED_PREFIX=0，并对共享前缀流量添加输出质量金丝雀。
  • 针对断开连接引发的故障进行加固。 #39216 是客户端 abort 时整引擎崩溃，#44369 可能卡死传输 worker。网关应对连接错误进行重试，但要预期有一部分 abort 会导致整个副本宕机 — 运行 N+1 容量并自动化重启。
  • Agentic 工作负载有两个独立风险。 GLM-5.3-Flash 在多工具提示下（#36669）和 DFLASH 投机解码下（#40843）都会退化；为这些路由添加重复看门狗或禁用 DFLASH。另外，工具 schema 校验在 API 事件循环上每个工具约耗时 0.7 ms，因此 10–20 工具的 agent 在生成开始前要付出 7–14 ms（#43274 是审查中的修复）。
  • SM120 部署是实战检验最少的路径。 多份独立报告都给出相同建议：triton 是可靠的 attention 后端，fa4 会破坏 CUDA-graph capture，且 GLM-5.3-Flash 在投产前仍需要一组修复（#42012、#37813、#40877）。
  • 如果你使用 AMD/MI355X，有低成本收益可拿 — FP8 quant+GEMM 融合（#42229）正针对交互式 agent 所处的低并发 EAGLE decode 场景。

  • b11642 — 服务器现在仅将可恢复的 slot 状态保存到提示缓存；与 rerank/embedding/completion 的 slot 行为相关 (b11642, PR #30498)。
  • 未明确列出 API 破坏性变更。如果你依赖提示缓存和嵌入图行为，请检查这些路径。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • Muse Spark Open — 文本/视觉/音频，潜在空间 MoE，残差 8192，4096 中 256 个专家，top-8 sigmoid 路由 (PR #30616)。
  • maion-coder — 新架构及 draft-model 接线；移除了上下文移位函数 (PR #29778)。
  • K2 Horizon / Prism / GLM5-Next MTP — 包含在 v0.7.0 模型批次中 (v0.7.0)。
  • Metal — 新增 tensor API flash-attention 内核的 BF16 变体，移至 kernels/fa_tensor.metal (PR #30491)。
  • Hexagon — 重构张量重打包，支持 tiled/flat 量化及 FP 权重 (PR #30635)；提议支持 Q1_0 (PR #30122)。
  • Vulkan/AMD — 跨步 f16 KV 拷贝仅执行一次，使读取分散到各内存通道 (PR #27703)。
  • mtmd/audio — 新增 mtmd_audio_stream 和 voxtral-realtime 支持 (PR #30629)。
  • 量化工具 — gguf-py 支持 Q1_0/Q2_0 numpy 反量化/量化 (PR #30630, issue #30626)。
  • 转换 — pplx-decider 支持纯文本检查点 (PR #30575)；修复 Granite Switch 块数问题 (PR #30621, issue #30617)；修复 Granite speech conv_norm 映射回归 (PR #30628)。

4. 性能与优化

  • MoE 主机缓存 — v0.7.0 中的 --moe-cache-mib 在专家被卸载时可提供最高 约 2.2 倍解码 (v0.7.0)。
  • 投机解码 — v0.7.0 新增 LiliCorr 和 GLM5-Next MTP (v0.7.0)。
  • Vulkan — 修复并发首设备初始化；测试现在并行加载模型以覆盖该场景 (PR #29766)。
  • Vulkan/AMD — f16 KV 跨步拷贝减少内存通道热点 (PR #27703)。
  • Metal — BF16 tensor-API flash attention 内核提升 BF16 路径覆盖 (PR #30491)。
  • 服务器提示缓存 — 仅保存可恢复的 slot 状态，减少 rerank/embedding 任务造成的缓存污染 (PR #30498)。
  • --moe-cache-topk — 已关闭的 PR 提议限制主机缓存 MoE 层上的活跃专家数 (PR #30593)。
  • Vulkan FA 反量化 — PR 检查合并后的 K+V f16 暂存区大小是否超过设备限制 (PR #30487)。
  • 回归观察 — draft-MTP 在多 GPU 层拆分时使提示处理大约减半 (issue #27428)；Vulkan 多设备 + CPU-MoE 的提示处理在 #29741 后变慢 (issue #30547)；qwen35 在 RTX 5090 上于原生 Linux 达到约 76% roofline (issue #28196)。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序：

  • 严重 — Metal 段错误：Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 在 Metal 上于 ggml_metal_op_mul_mat_id 崩溃 (issue #30610)。
  • 严重 — llama-server VRAM DoS：服务器在某些请求下可能耗尽 VRAM (issue #30577)。
  • 严重 — 内存 DoS：客户端设置的 X-Conversation-Id 会禁用断开连接取消，并累积无上限的可恢复流会话 (issue #29498)。
  • 高 — MTP 提示处理回归：draft-MTP 在多 GPU 层拆分时使 PP 减半；单 GPU 正常 (issue #27428)。
  • 高 — Vulkan 提示处理缓慢：多设备 + cpu-moe MoE 在 #29741 后出现回归 (issue #30547)。
  • 高 — launch_fattn 中的断言：RX6950XT 上的 HIP/ROCm (issue #27674)。
  • 高 — Vulkan MTP 断言：在张量拆分下进行投机 draft 解码时出现 GGML_ASSERT(neq0 == HSK) (issue #29418)。
  • 高 — CUDA 地址未对齐：RTX 5090 Laptop 上长提示触发 ggml_cuda_op_unary<op_sigmoid> (issue #28877)。
  • 高 — Vulkan 生成极慢：自 b11594 以来出现性能回归 (issue #30552)。
  • 今日已修复/关闭：Vulkan MiniMax-M2 在长上下文/ubatch >128 时提示崩溃 (issue #30364)；Granite Switch 转换块数错误 (issue #30617, 修复 PR #30621)；slot KV 恢复空操作 (issue #26676)；rerank 提示缓存内存增长 (issue #26293)。
  • 进行中的修复 PR：SYCL IQ3 崩溃修复 (PR #30604)；组合 draft-MTP + 外部 draft 初始化崩溃 (PR #27897, 相关 issue #27839)；Vulkan FA 反量化合并 K+V 暂存区检查 (PR #30487)。

6. 对应用开发者的意义

  • 升级到 v0.7.0 以获得 MoE 卸载和投机解码，但由于多 GPU 提示处理回归，生产环境前需在多 GPU 上验证 MTP (issue #27428)。
  • 服务器 API 正在扩展：提议通过 /v1/realtime WebSocket 实现实时转录 (PR #30636)；embeddings dimensions 支持已在 PR 中 (PR #24898, issue #25210)；提议 HF 模型发现/下载 UI (PR #29584)。
  • 提示缓存行为已变更 — 仅保存可恢复的 slot 状态，因此 rerank/embedding 工作负载不应再污染 completion 缓存 (PR #30498)。
  • 新模型集成需要检查模板 — K2 Horizon 在低/中推理强度下可能将最终文本/工具调用留在 reasoning_content 中 (issue #30246)；Qwen3-Coder 推理/内容分隔符修复仍开放 (PR #30557)。
  • 后端运维者应谨慎固定版本/测试：Metal 存在 MoE 段错误 (issue #30610)；Vulkan 存在 MTP/tensor-split 和 CPU-MoE 回归 (issue #29418, issue #30547)；CUDA sm_120 存在长提示 sigmoid 问题 (issue #28877)。
  • 面向不可信客户端的部署应缓解 DoS 风险：VRAM 耗尽 (issue #30577) 以及通过 X-Conversation-Id 导致的可恢复流内存增长 (issue #29498)。
  • 量化/工具收益：Q1_0/Q2_0 numpy 支持改进 gguf-py 工作流 (PR #30630)；Hexagon Q1_0 和重打包工作仍在继续 (PR #30122, PR #30635)。
Ollama — ollama/ollama

Ollama 摘要 — 2026-10-16

1. 今日亮点

过去 24 小时内没有新版本发布，但 issue 跟踪器主要被 agent/tool-calling 正确性问题 和 模型拉取回归 占据：据报告，原生 POST /api/chat 路径会在工具定义到达模型之前将其剥离，而多个 0.40.x 用户无法通过 SOCKS 代理拉取模型，或反复遇到重定向/重试失败。积极的一面是，上游 llama.cpp 集成工作取得进展——MiniCPM-V 4.7 projector 支持和 Q2_0 量化均有修复 PR，GGUF v4 解析改进（64KB DMA 对齐）也已提出。

2. 发布与破坏性变更

过去 24 小时内没有发布任何版本。以下为进行中 PR 的背景信息：

  • llama.cpp 升级至 b11669 (#19032, 已关闭) — 底层运行时变更；注意，正是 b11669 启用了 Q2_0 GGUF 支持。
  • Q2_0 GGUF 张量/文件类型支持 (#18967, 已关闭) — 此前 ollama create/模型加载会失败并报 unsupported tensor "token_embd.weight" size overflows；新增张量类型 42 / 文件类型 41（64 个权重，每块 18 字节）。在旧版本上导入的现有 Q2_0 GGUF 将需要新运行时。
  • 未宣布任何 API/配置弃用或迁移步骤。（#8018 —— 将 /delete 改为 POST —— 是一个旧的、已关闭的 PR，并非当前变更。）

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • MiniCPM-V 4.7 (openbmb/minicpm-v4.7:35b-a3b) — 加载失败 unknown projector type: minicpmv4_7 (#18983, 已关闭) 已通过将固定的 llama.cpp 从 b11521 → b11551 更新修复 (#19024)。
  • Q2_0 量化 — GGUF reader 现已理解 Q2_0 (#18967)；这对极低位模型导入（例如 Prism ML 发布）很重要。
  • GGUF v4 规范 — 提议为 GPU DMA 引入 64KB（65536）页对齐，以实现零拷贝张量映射，并支持 O(1) token-span seek (#19037)。
  • 视觉模型 — 新增 Clippy Vision (#19033)。
  • 云 — Clef 现已在 Ollama Cloud 上可用 (#19036)。
  • 后端说明 — 没有新的 CUDA/ROCm/Metal 后端支持落地；若干 ROCm/CUDA 问题仍处于开放状态（见下文）。

4. 性能与优化

  • CPU 线程/cgroup 不匹配 — n_threads 由宿主机核心数推导，忽略 cgroup v2 cpu.max 和 cpuset。在 CPU 受限容器中，这会导致自旋等待与 CFS 节流形成护送效应，据报告造成 约 45 倍吞吐量崩塌。(#17916)
  • MLX 引擎为单请求串行 — 无论 OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL 如何设置，请求都严格按 FIFO 处理，没有连续批处理。一个 issue 已关闭 (#17666)，而批处理/并行解码的功能请求仍处于开放状态 (#17280, 👍 4)。
  • 回归报告：文本分类器模型在 0.40.4 上比 0.40.3 更慢（nimble、clef-flash、tev1）— 尚未确认，需要基准测试。(#19002)
  • GGUF v4 seek/对齐 — 提议 64KB DMA 对齐和 O(1) 批量 token-span 丢弃，以加快模型检查/模型操作。(#19037)

5. 稳定性与回归（按严重程度排序）

严重 — 正确性/数据完整性

  • 云端生成退化：glm-5.3-flash:cloud 有 5–8% 的请求失败，并报告出现宿主机侧数据区域被清零。长期存在，22 条评论，未关联修复。(#18980)
  • 原生 /api/chat 在整个安装范围内将工具定义渲染为空 — 模型会回显 {"name": ""}/{{ <nil> <nil> [] {}}}，且从不发出 tool_calls；/v1 能正确渲染工具。对 agent 影响很大。(#19040)
  • Go API 工具调用参数会静默丢失数值精度（普通 + 流式路径）— 已有修复 PR。(#18942, fix #18941)

高 — 崩溃/挂起

  • RTX 5090 上的 CUDA 非法内存访问（MUL_MAT）：Windows 上运行 Cohere MoE 时发生，随后 llama-server 崩溃（0xc0000409）。(#18642)
  • ROCm：gemma4:26b-a4b 在将 experts 卸载到 CPU 时于 hipGraphInstantiate 中中止（OOM），随后每次加载都发生段错误；变通方案为 GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1。(#19015)
  • Qwen3.5 推理期间发生 A100 PCIe 总线丢失（Xid79）：出现在 0.34.4/0.35.0 上，需要整节点重启恢复。(#19006)
  • 解析器在孤立分隔符工具调用值上 panic（value[8:0] 切片越界）— 修复 PR 开放中。(#17492)
  • 工具调用开标签在流式分块边界处丢失（DeepSeek3、Cogito、LFM2 解析器）— 修复 PR 通过 219 个测试。(#19028)
  • gemma4 在 think: false 时于工具响应后返回空回复 — 空 thought 块从未关闭。(#18861)

中 — 拉取/传输与启动

  • 自 0.40.4 起，ollama pull 在使用 SOCKS 代理时失效（0.34.4 上正常）— 已关闭。(#19035)
  • 拉取失败：redirect target not allowed / R2 端点 DNS 解析 (#18716) 以及 max retries exceeded (#18842)。
  • blob 下载期间磁盘已满却被误报为成功 — 传输层忽略了写入错误；修复 PR 开放中。(#18813)
  • 回归：timed out waiting for llama-server to start：使用 virtio-gpu/drm 原生上下文时出现；0.32.9 正常，0.32.10+ 损坏。(#18123)

低 — 桌面/API 边缘情况

  • Windows 托盘应用在端口 11434 已被占用时，会永远约每秒启动一次 ollama serve。(#19013)
  • 桌面应用内存泄漏 — 上下文菜单标签 C 字符串被分配后从未释放。(#19029)
  • 云端 mistral-large-4 在 /v1/responses 上以 HTTP 400 拒绝 role: "developer"，阻塞 Codex 风格客户端。(#19021)
  • bge-m3 embedding 在某些 UTF-8 markdown 文件上返回 HTTP 500 json: unsupported value: NaN。(#15582)
  • 依赖公告（SCA）：seroval fromJSON() Promise resolver 类型混淆 — 已在 ≥1.5.3 中修补。(#19034)
  • Windows 上缺少 Claude Desktop 开关。 (#18164)

6. 这对应用开发者意味着什么

  • 目前，对于工具调用 agent，优先使用 /v1 而非原生 /api/chat。 据报告，原生路由会清空工具定义，而 OpenAI 兼容路由能正确渲染它们 (#19040)。在发布前端到端验证工具 schema。
  • 当 Go 客户端往返工具调用参数时，警惕静默数值截断 — 应用待合并的修复，或添加你自己的无损解码 (#18942)。
  • 流式解析器正在被加固，以处理分块边界标签拆分和孤立分隔符 panic；如果你运行 DeepSeek3、Cogito、LFM2 或 FunctionGemma 模型，请在这些修复合并后固定到包含它们的构建 (#19028, #17492)。
  • Responses-API 兼容性正在改善：现在历史记录中容忍来自外部提供商的 compaction 项 (#19003)，并且对于非思考模型会忽略过期的 reasoning.effort (#19010) — 如果你在会话中途切换模型，这很有用。
  • 容器化部署：显式设置 OLLAMA_NUM_THREADS。 默认值忽略 cgroup 配额，在 CPU 受限的 pod 中可能造成高达约 45 倍的吞吐量损失 (#17916)。
  • 在 Apple Silicon 上，不要假设存在并发。 MLX runner 无论 OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL 如何都会将请求串行化；请据此设计你的排队/背压 (#17280)。
  • 关注云可靠性：如果你通过 Ollama Cloud 路由，注意 glm-5.3-flash:cloud（报告 5–8% 失败率）和 mistral-large-4 拒绝 developer 角色的问题 (#18980, #19021)。
  • 低位与多模态导入正在扩展 — Q2_0 GGUF 支持 (#18967) 和 MiniCPM-V 4.7 (#19024) 都需要运行时更新；在生产环境中依赖它们之前，请分阶段升级。
LiteLLM — BerriAI/litellm

LiteLLM 摘要 — 2026-10-16

来源：BerriAI/litellm

1. 今日亮点

LiteLLM 仅有的新发布是预发布版 v1.107.0-dev.2 和 v1.106.0-rc.4，两者都聚焦于 cosign Docker 镜像签名验证，而非功能变更。最严重的未关闭报告仍然是 v1.82.3 中的预算执行绕过（#26672）、Kubernetes 上持续的 RAM 增长/OOM（#27954），以及未认证客户端通过失败的认证尝试虚增支出表（#42689）。进行中的 PR 工作集中在 Rust/原生路由与 Python 的对齐（#46764, #46788, #46787）、重试/退避正确性（#46730）、WebSocket 支出核算（#46768），以及通过 ID-JAG/JWT-bearer 实现 MCP 跨应用访问（#46748, #46747, #46745）。

2. 发布与破坏性变更

  • v1.107.0-dev.2 — dev 预发布版；发布说明仅涵盖 Docker cosign 验证。发布
  • v1.106.0-rc.4 — RC 预发布版；同样的 cosign 验证说明。发布
  • 发布说明中未描述破坏性 API/配置变更。运维提示：所有 LiteLLM Docker 镜像均使用 cosign 签名；请使用 commit 0112e53 中的密钥进行验证。
  • 留意尚未发布、即将到来的行为变更：重试将遵循 Retry-After，并使用指数退避+抖动，同时过滤瞬时错误（#46730）；token 计数新增 litellm_count_source / litellm_count_fallback_model 以及可配置 framing（#46777）；Rust 的 /v1/messages 和 /v1/responses body-param 过滤向 Python 规则靠拢（#46764, #46788, #46787）。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • 本窗口期内没有新的 CUDA/ROCm/Metal/CPU 后端、加速器或量化格式。
  • Bedrock Claude Platform：PR #46670 在 web identity 会话策略中授予 sts:GetWebIdentityToken 和 sts:TagGetWebIdentityToken，修复 OIDC 认证的 403。
  • OpenAI 音频：PR #44021 将 gpt-transcribe 路由到 GPT 音频转录配置；修复缺少 response_format 导致的 400 和健康检查失败。
  • Anthropic：PR #46754 在 /v1/responses 上将 Anthropic compaction 块以 compaction item 形式往返传递，防止重复进行全历史摘要。
  • Token 计数：PR #46777 新增可配置的 token_count_framing 和 token_count_fallback_model，以及计数来源报告；针对 Bedrock Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 的 404 和 Kimi K3 / DeepSeek 的估算 framing。
  • Router 上下文：PR #46197 允许在成本映射一致时，由精确的 base_model 放宽部署的上下文窗口。
  • 仍开放的模型/后端 bug：Databricks gpt-5.6 系列 tool + reasoning_effort（#43708）；带 openai/ 前缀的自托管模型在 /v1/messages 上被路由到 Responses API，破坏多模态（#40780）。已关闭：Moonshot/Kimi K2.6 reasoning-content 工具调用问题（#26156）；OCI Grok/coding-agent 工具 schema 问题（#31449）。

4. 性能与优化

  • CLI 冷启动：PR #46803 启动 lite/litellm-proxy 时不再导入完整 LiteLLM SDK；在 1 CPU VM 上避免约 3,000 个模块和 1.5–4 秒，有客户案例报告每条命令最高可达 20 秒。
  • 网关负载测试：PR #46806 新增负载测试套件、Docker 构建开关和 TCP_NODELAY；FAST=1 跳过 LTO，将构建时间从约 13 分钟降至约 5 分钟。
  • 每请求性能核算：PR #46798 使 postgres_calls_per_request 和 redis_calls_per_request 变为每请求统计，而非整服务器总计；PR #46774 将性能指标/限制导出为 JUnit 属性。
  • 重试行为：PR #46730 将近乎瞬时重试（<0.2ms）替换为感知 Retry-After 的指数退避+抖动，并过滤 401 等不可恢复错误。
  • 缓存：issue #28427 已关闭 — prompt-caching router affinity TTL 被硬编码为 5 分钟，破坏了 1 小时临时缓存路由。
  • 内存压力：issue #27954 仍开放 — Kubernetes 中 LiteLLM pod 会达到 RAM 上限并随时间崩溃；在修复落地前请持续监控。
  • WebSocket 支出：PR #46768 对每个原生 Responses WebSocket 轮次写入一条 spend-log 记录，而不是在 socket 关闭时写一条，避免 pod 重启时丢失支出。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序。

严重

  • #27954 开放 — 严重的 RAM 增长导致 Kubernetes pod OOM/崩溃；8 👍。未引用修复 PR。
  • #26672 开放 — v1.82.3 中，key/user 的 max_budget 预算执行被绕过，即使支出超过限制。
  • #42689 开放 — 每次使用未知 key 的失败认证都会写入各自的支出行，因此未认证客户端可以虚增用量表。
  • #26399 已关闭 — Bedrock passthrough 路由绕过了 key.models / user.models 允许列表。

高

  • #38358 开放 — 当上游接受 TCP 但不发送首字节时，litellm_settings.request_timeout 从不触发。
  • #32357 开放 — /v1/messages 适配器错误编码推理模型：文本块内的 thinking_delta 和重复的 message_start 导致 Anthropic SDK / Claude Code 内容为空。
  • #31909 开放 — mcp_semantic_tool_filter 会为标准的嵌套 OpenAI tools 格式剥离所有工具。
  • #46403 已关闭 — 当提供商复用响应 ID（Ollama chatcmpl-<0..999>）时，SpendLogs 行被静默丢弃；request_id 主键冲突。
  • #46407 开放 — gpt-image 成本忽略 EU 数据驻留加价和部署级 output_cost_per_image_token。
  • #40780 开放 — 带 openai/ 前缀的自托管模型将 /v1/messages 路由到 Responses API，静默丢失多模态支持。
  • #43708 开放 — 在 /chat/completions 上，Databricks 托管的 gpt-5.6 系列函数工具因 reasoning_effort 错误而失败。

中 / 启动与 MCP

  • #30425 开放 — 配置数据库后，代理启动时出现 Failed to import Prisma client。
  • #33431 开放 — 编辑配置中的 MCP 服务器身份字段会静默孤立现有授权。
  • #33492 开放 — OpenAPI-spec MCP 无法将 extra_headers 转发到上游后端。
  • #33671 开放 — 独立 Bedrock Guardrails 集成从不发送 AWS trace 参数，丢失评估细节。
  • #46764 审查中的高风险 PR — Rust /v1/messages body-param 对齐；#46788, #46787 为较低风险的 Rust 桥接对齐工作。

窗口期内已关闭的正确性修复

  • #25429 chatgpt/gpt-5.4 最终 Responses 输出为空 / completion bridge 失败。
  • #14004 当预算超限时，免费/无成本自托管模型被阻止。
  • #31447 team_member_budget 替换了整个团队元数据对象。
  • #27038 disable_end_user_cost_tracking 未控制 SpendLogs / DailyEndUserSpend 写入。
  • #31587 当 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY 缺失/无效时，/v1/skills 返回 500。
  • #26156 Moonshot/Kimi K2.6 多轮工具调用丢失 reasoning_content。
  • #27184 Bedrock Claude 4.6 tool_choice.type required 错误。
  • #37175 Anthropic /v1/messages → Responses 适配器丢弃图像 detail 并错误标记 thinking。
  • #31449 来自 coding agents 的 OCI 提供商工具请求失败。
  • #28444 Post API hook 未对 passthrough 端点启用。
  • #24628 S3 文件名过长。
  • #25456 Chat completions → Responses bridge 未处理带 URL 的 file_id。
  • #25191 通过 /chat/completions 访问 Bedrock 时未触发 websearch_interception。
  • #45411 尽管 Bedrock Invoke 支持，Claude Code 的 per-turn-control 仍对 Bedrock 被过滤。

6. 这对应用开发者意味着什么

  • 预算/成本安全：如果你依赖预算、免费模型路由或终端用户支出跟踪，请针对 #26672、#14004、#42689、#46403、#46407 进行验证。为 SpendLogs 增长和 request-ID 冲突添加告警。
  • Claude Code / Anthropic SDK：将 /v1/messages 视为仍在稳定中。跟踪 #32357、#40780、#37175，以及 Rust 对齐 PR #46764、#46788。在 #40780 修复前，避免通过 /v1/messages 使用带 openai/ 前缀的自托管多模态模型。
  • MCP/agents：ID-JAG/JWT-bearer 和 SSO 断言捕获即将到来（#46748, #46747, #46745），但在生产前请验证工具过滤（#31909）和 MCP 身份/请求头行为（#33431, #33492）。
  • 网关可运维性：预计 CLI 启动（#46803）、重试（#46730）、WebSocket 支出核算（#46768）和负载测试工具（#46806）会更好。对于 Kubernetes，请监控 RAM 增长（#27954）。
  • Bedrock/模型兼容性：使用 #46670 处理 Claude Platform web identity；关注 #33671 的 Guardrails trace、#43708 的 Databricks gpt-5.6，以及 #46777 的 token 计数。
  • Docker 供应链：对于 v1.106/v1.107 系列镜像，请使用 commit 0112e53 中的密钥验证 cosign 签名。
Unsloth — unslothai/unsloth

Unsloth 摘要 — 2026-10-16

1. 今日亮点

Unsloth 发布了 v0.1.908-beta，新增 NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5（包括可在 24 GB 内存上运行的 Bolt 变体）和 Meta Muse Spark Open，并加入文本扩散 LLM 支持、DeepSpeed 训练，以及为编码 agent 改进的提示词缓存。同一时间窗口还出现了一批密集的 Studio 基础设施 PR，目标包括多 GPU 放置、NVIDIA MIG 掩码、AMD 安装器路由和 ROCm attention 选择——其中许多仍处于开放和审查中。在 issue tracker 上，若干长期存在的 AMD/Studio bug 已关闭，而模型重新加载后的 KV-cache 持久化和多 GPU 微调仍然开放。

2. 发布与破坏性变更

  • v0.1.908-beta — NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 + Meta Muse Spark Open：新的模型家族、文本扩散 LLM、DeepSpeed 训练支持、为编码 agent 提供更好的提示词缓存。Beta 通道，因此请视为尚未固定用于生产。
  • 安全/依赖基线已变动 — PR #13949 将 pip scan-packages 审计的基线重设为 unsloth-zoo 2026.10.6 和 transformers 5.20.0。上游文件变更使固定的扫描条目失效；如果你使用自有的审计门禁从源码构建，预计需要重设基线。
  • TRL 兼容性收窄 — PR #13911 除非 fast_inference 共享权重，否则将 TRL 的 vLLM 权重同步限制在 TRL < 0.28。之前的行为会在 TRL 0.22–0.27 上无条件将 GRPOTrainer._move_model_to_vllm 置为空操作，而这仅在 fast_inference=True 时才正确。如果你固定 TRL 版本，这一点很重要。
  • 本时间窗口未宣布任何公共 API 或配置弃用。

3. 新模型与硬件支持

  • NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 / Nemotron 3.5 “Bolt” — 可在 24 GB 内存上运行；指南见 unsloth.ai/docs/models/nemotron。
  • Meta Muse Spark Open — 同一 beta 版本中支持本地运行。
  • 文本扩散 LLM — v0.1.908-beta 中新增一等路径。
  • FLUX.3 Image Klein（distilled + base）、INT8/FP8/GGUF — PR #13933 添加对 black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein[-base] 的加载支持，这些模型仅以 Modular Diffusers blocks 形式提供（modular_model_index.json，而非 model_index.json）。
  • 旧版仓库的 4-bit 回退 — PR #13941 修复了 Tulu-3-8B/70B、SOLAR-10.7B、OpenThinker-7B、Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-405B、Pixtral-12B 在默认 4-bit 加载时的 “repository not found”，通过回退到基础模型实现。
  • AMD/ROCm：针对 Strix APU + 独立显卡组合的安装器路由修复（PR #13931）、Windows hipinfo 双重掩码修复（PR #13925），以及 MIG 掩码/切片感知的大小计算（PR #13927）。
  • 已请求但尚未支持：Cohere Command A+ 218B/A25B（#5952，已关闭，未注明已支持）。

4. 性能与优化

  • 并发聊天的 KV 抢占 — PR #10301：并行聊天共享一个 KV cache；llama-server 通过 --preempt-ram 负责停放/暂存，取代了每个聊天各自完整预填充的模式。这是对 #9037 中长期上下文重新预填充问题的结构性修复。
  • ROCm flash attention 选择 — PR #13792 用整块计时探测取代硬编码的模型族表，因此可在 gfx11（例如 Strix Halo gfx1151）上为任意模型形状选用 flash_attn，而不是总是回退到 torch SDPA/AOTriton。
  • 编译下的 MoE 4-bit 反量化 — PR #13946 在 UNSLOTH_MOE_SELECTIVE_DEQUANT=1 / UNSLOTH_MOE_DEQUANT_CHUNK_EXPERTS=N 时，将选择启用的 bnb 4-bit MoE experts 保持在 torch.compile 块之外。
  • 混合代际 NVIDIA 主机 — PR #13923 根据所有可见 GPU 而非仅 device 0 来决定 bfloat16、compile 和 TMA，修复异构节点上静默的能力不匹配。
  • GPU 放置 — PR #13928 让图像/视频自动加载选择最空闲的 GPU，而不是 PCI slot 0。
  • Chat UI — PR #13919 通过默认禁用代码行窗口化来修复滚动条卡死。
  • 版本层面：v0.1.908-beta 中的 DeepSpeed 训练路径，以及为编码 agent 重构的提示词缓存。

5. 稳定性与回归

按严重程度排序；若干高严重性项已有修复或已关闭。

  1. ROCm 预编译二进制在 hipStreamCreateWithFlags 处因 OOM 崩溃 — #12205（已关闭）：b11160-mix-a6922cc 的预编译 linux/rocm 资产会失败，而 同一 提交的源码构建则可正常工作。已由 AMD 安装器/架构路由 PR（#13931、#13925）缓解。
  2. Studio 多 GPU 大小计算错误与加载到错误显卡 — MIG UUID 掩码被当作“无掩码”，导致按完整的 40/80 GB 卡计算大小（#13927）；图像/视频自动加载跑在繁忙的 device 0 上（#13928）。修复 PR 开放中。
  3. 长聊天在模型重新加载后重做完整预填充 — #9037（开放中）：slot KV 仅在空闲自动卸载时持久化。没有已合并的修复；#10301 是预期的补救方案。
  4. 共享本地服务器上的多账号模型同步失败 — #12365（已关闭）：当前加载的模型在局域网用户之间无法保持一致。
  5. Qwen-Image-2.1 编辑期间 diffusion_prompt_cache.py 中出现 CUBLAS 错误 — #13638（已关闭）。
  6. Strix Halo（Windows）默认使用 Vulkan，预填充缓慢 — #10656 和 #5405（均已关闭）：GPU 未充分利用，或在 Docker 中回退到 CPU。
  7. AMD Docker 容器在 CPU 而非 Strix Halo APU 上运行 — #5405（已关闭）。
  8. Windows MXC Sandbox 启用失败，且说明不清晰 — #13656（开放中，未固定）。
  9. Model Hub 适配过滤器泄漏超出预算的模型 — #13945（修复开放中）以及过滤器行为 bug #13613（已关闭）。
  10. Vision-Wayland/NVIDIA 合成 — #13892（已关闭）：优先使用 dmabuf 而非静态关闭合成，以避免 Wayland Error 71。
  11. 通过未列出的命令逃逸沙箱 — PR #13942（开放中）：在“Approve for me”下，ffmpeg/pandoc 绝对路径写到了沙箱之外，因为只检查了 cp/mv。应将 agent 沙箱视为尚不严密。
  12. Embeddinggemma-2 文件嵌入在索引阶段失败 — #13663（已关闭）。

6. 这对应用开发者意味着什么

  • 24 GB 的 Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 是可行的单张消费级 GPU 服务目标。 如果你正在为基于 Nemotron/Muse Spark 的 agent 规划推理主机，24 GB 档位现在是下限，而不再是 48–80 GB 显卡。
  • 并行聊天/会话服务是当前活跃的工作流。 #10301 转向由一个 llama-server 持有一个 KV cache，并带抢占/停放机制。如果你在一个 Studio 实例上复用许多 agent 会话，预计每会话的有效上下文将取决于抢占策略——在该功能落地前，请有意固定你的 Studio 版本。
  • 同构 GPU 假设并不安全。 #13923 和 #13927 都修复了此前仅依据 device 0 或整卡 VRAM 做出的决策。在混合代际或 MIG 分区的集群上，不要相信修复前构建的自动放置。
  • AMD 支持正在改善，但在安装时仍然脆弱。 Strix Halo CPU 回退和 ROCm OOM bug 已关闭，但修复属于安装器/架构路由变更——请重新构建或重新运行安装器，而不是复用现有的 ROCm wheels。
  • 通过 Studio 进行多 GPU 微调仍在路线图上，尚未发布。 #5764 处于开放状态并标记为 on roadmap；目前请使用带 device_map 的 Python API 进行多卡 LoRA。
  • 偏好调优的功能对等性仍是缺口。 #5291 请求将 GRPO 的分块/隐藏状态优化移植到 ORPO/DPO/CPO——请为这些训练器预留比 GRPO 更多的 VRAM。
  • 沙箱尚不是安全边界。 在 #13942 合并之前，不要依赖“Approve for me”模式来约束通过任意二进制文件写入的工具命令。
  • 本周期工具链固定很重要：transformers 5.20.0 和 TRL < 0.28 的行为变更正在进行中；请在 CI 中显式冻结它们。

本日报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-10-16

Generated: 2026-10-16 00:40 UTC | Projects covered: 6

  • vLLM
  • SGLang
  • llama.cpp
  • Ollama
  • LiteLLM
  • Unsloth

Cross-Project Comparison

Cross-Project AI Infrastructure Comparison — 2026-10-16

1. Ecosystem Overview

AI infrastructure activity remains extremely high, but the center of gravity has shifted from raw throughput to correctness, cache safety, and agent/tool reliability. Serving engines are racing to support DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3, Qwen3.x, Kimi K3, Muse Spark Open, and Nemotron 3.5 across GB300, Blackwell SM120, ROCm/MI355X, and Apple/consumer hardware. At the same time, several high-severity issues are silent correctness bugs — stale KV in PD disaggregation, prefix-cache cross-request contamination, stripped tool definitions, and gateway budget/spend bypasses. Stable releases are limited: llama.cpp shipped v0.7.0, Unsloth shipped a beta, LiteLLM shipped prereleases, and vLLM/SGLang/Ollama had no new releases in this window.

2. Activity Comparison

N/R = digest does not disclose 24h totals. Counts are reported "updated in last 24h" where available.

Project Issues updated (24h) PRs updated (24h) Release status
vLLM 121 500 No new releases; no formal breaking changes
SGLang N/R N/R No new releases; Python 3.10 removal in progress; no API removals
llama.cpp 47 149 v0.7.0 / b11669; b11671 Muse Spark Open; b11658 maion-coder; b11662; b11643; b11642
Ollama N/R N/R No releases in last 24h
LiteLLM N/R N/R v1.107.0-dev.2, v1.106.0-rc.4 prereleases; cosign Docker verification
Unsloth N/R N/R v0.1.908-beta

Readout: vLLM and llama.cpp disclose the largest raw update volumes. vLLM is PR-heavy and correctness-focused; llama.cpp is shipping release content. SGLang is dominated by CI/stability and SM120/GLM-5.3 issues. Ollama, LiteLLM, and Unsloth show concentrated activity around agent/tool correctness, gateway operability, and training/model onboarding respectively.

3. Model Support Race

Shipped / landed support:

  • llama.cpp: v0.7.0 adds GLM5-Next MTP, K2 Horizon dense/MoVA, Prism, and host-memory MoE expert cache. b11671 adds Muse Spark Open text/vision/audio. b11658 adds maion-coder plus draft-model support.
  • Unsloth: v0.1.908-beta adds NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 / Bolt (24 GB), Meta Muse Spark Open, text-diffusion LLMs, DeepSpeed training, and improved prompt caching for coding agents. FLUX.3 Image Klein loading is in PR.
  • Ollama: MiniCPM-V 4.7 projector support fixed via llama.cpp bump; Q2_0 GGUF support added; Clippy Vision and Clef Cloud added.
  • LiteLLM: Not a model-kernel project, but provider compatibility advanced for Bedrock Claude web identity, OpenAI gpt-transcribe, Anthropic compaction blocks, Bedrock Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 token counting, Kimi K3 / DeepSeek framing, and Databricks gpt-5.6 tool/reasoning issues.

In-flight / not yet released:

  • vLLM: Muse Spark Open, Step-5-Preview on ROCm, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GB300 low-latency decode, ROCm fused QK-norm + RoPE + gate kernels. Nemotron 3.5 ASR streaming, Phi4Flash, and ViT full CUDA graph are requests/RFCs.
  • SGLang: SM120 field reports for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; GLM-5.3-Flash SM120 tracking; Hopper CuTe DSL KDA verify kernel; AMD AITER/DSv4 GEMM work; Muse Spark Open NIXL KV packing.

Who is ahead?

  • Breadth of shipped local model support: llama.cpp and Unsloth are ahead.
  • Data-center serving enablement on new accelerators: vLLM and SGLang are ahead, especially for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3, ROCm/MI355X, and GB300/SM120.
  • Provider/API compatibility: LiteLLM is ahead.
  • Agentic correctness: Ollama is currently behind due to native /api/chat tool-definition issues.

4. Performance Frontier

Optimization effort is concentrated in five areas:

KV cache and prefix caching

  • vLLM: PD disaggregation prefix-cache contamination, KV connector cache validity, model-customized KVCache planning, Mamba block-size regression.
  • SGLang: HiCache stale-KV silent corruption, unified memory pool prewarm/compaction, NIXL KV packing.
  • llama.cpp: prompt cache now saves only restorable slot states; --moe-cache-mib host expert cache.
  • Unsloth: KV preemption for concurrent chats, prompt caching for coding agents.

Batching and decode latency

  • vLLM: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash GB300 low-latency decode, DSpark speculative decoding, FA2 short-query/long-context attention.
  • SGLang: AMD FP8 quant+GEMM fusion for EAGLE low-concurrency decode, PP-spec compare skipping.
  • Ollama: MLX engine remains single-request serial; no continuous batching.
  • Unsloth: parallel chat serving via llama-server KV parking/preemption.

Quantization and low-bit formats

  • llama.cpp: Q1_0/Q2_0 numpy support, Hexagon Q1_0 proposal, repacking rework.
  • Ollama: Q2_0 GGUF tensor/file-type support.
  • Unsloth: 4-bit MoE dequant under compile, FLUX.3 INT8/FP8/GGUF.
  • vLLM/SGLang: NVFP4 OOM, W4A16 routed experts, FP8 KV.

Distributed serving

  • vLLM: TP4 + DSpark, PD disaggregation, MoE exact strides, hybrid GDN prefix-cache hits.
  • SGLang: NIXL TP-heterogeneous transfer, PD prefill + HiCache, DCP planner crashes.
  • llama.cpp: MTP multi-GPU prompt-processing regression; Vulkan multi-device + CPU-MoE slowdown.
  • LiteLLM: Gateway load testing, retry/backoff, WebSocket spend accounting, Rust route parity.

Kernels

  • vLLM: FA2 optimization, ROCm Triton fused kernels, Mamba2 NaN fixes.
  • SGLang: AMD FP8 GEMM fusion, CuTe DSL KDA verify on Hopper, deepstack CUDA-graph handling.
  • llama.cpp: Metal BF16 tensor-API flash attention, Vulkan f16 KV striding, Hexagon tensor repacking.
  • Unsloth: ROCm flash attention timing probe, MoE dequant outside torch.compile, mixed-generation GPU capability detection.

5. Layer Positioning

Layer Projects Primary concern Today’s signal
Serving engine vLLM, SGLang High-throughput distributed GPU inference, paged attention, PD disaggregation, speculative decoding Correctness bugs in prefix cache/PD are the top risk; new hardware enablement is active
Local runtime llama.cpp, Ollama Single-node/desktop/edge inference, GGUF, broad hardware llama.cpp shipping MoE offload/spec decode; Ollama struggling with agent/tool-calling correctness
Gateway LiteLLM Multi-provider routing, auth, budgets, spend logs, retries, MCP Budget bypass, spend-table inflation, RAM/OOM, and /v1/messages compatibility are key risks
Training / fine-tuning Unsloth LoRA/RL/GRPO, model onboarding, Studio UI, AMD/NVIDIA support Beta support for Nemotron 3.5/Muse Spark; multi-GPU fine-tuning still roadmap, sandboxing not airtight

Overlaps: Ollama depends on llama.cpp/MLX underneath. Unsloth also touches inference/Studio serving. vLLM and SGLang are increasingly used for RL rollout and agent backends, which exposes them to training-loop correctness requirements.

6. Trend Signals

  1. Silent correctness is now the dominant infrastructure risk.
    vLLM’s PD prefix-cache crosstalk, SGLang’s HiCache stale-KV bug, Ollama’s stripped tool definitions, and LiteLLM’s budget/spend bypasses all fail without clear errors. Agent developers should add output canaries, disable risky prefix caching, and monitor spend tables.

  2. New model support velocity is highest in local runtimes and training stacks.
    llama.cpp and Unsloth shipped Muse Spark Open, Nemotron 3.5, GLM5-Next, K2 Horizon, and text-diffusion support. vLLM/SGLang are still enabling DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3, and Qwen3.x on new accelerators.

  3. Hardware diversification is accelerating — and so are hardware-specific regressions.
    GB300, Blackwell SM120, ROCm MI355X, Strix Halo, Vulkan, Metal, Hexagon, and MIG all appear. SM120 is explicitly “least-battle-tested”; multi-GPU heterogeneous and MIG decisions should not be trusted on pre-fix builds.

  4. Speculative decoding and MoE offload are the main performance levers — with regressions.
    vLLM DSpark, llama.cpp LiliCorr/MTP, SGLang EAGLE/DSPARK, and MoE host caching offer large gains, but MTP multi-GPU prompt processing and Vulkan MTP assertions are active regressions.

  5. Gateway operationalization is maturing.
    LiteLLM is adding retry/backoff, WebSocket spend accounting, load-test kits, CLI cold-start improvements, and Rust route parity. For production, cost/budget correctness and /v1/messages stability remain the watch items.

  6. Agent workloads are stressing every layer.
    Tool schema validation costs, streaming parser chunk-boundary bugs, GLM-5.3-Flash degeneration, sandbox escape risks, and empty tool definitions are all present. Prefer /v1 over Ollama native /api/chat for tool calling; validate strict/required/named tool choices in vLLM; and treat Unsloth sandboxing as not yet a security boundary.

  7. Pinning matters more than usual this cycle.
    SGLang is removing Python 3.10 for CUDA builds; Unsloth is rebaselining against transformers 5.20.0 and TRL < 0.28; LiteLLM prereleases are cosign-only; llama.cpp’s v0.7.0 changes prompt-cache and MTP behavior. Freeze versions deliberately in CI and production.

Per-Project Reports

vLLM — vllm-project/vllm

vLLM Digest — 2026-10-16

Activity snapshot: No new releases. 121 issues and 500 PRs were updated in the last 24h. Work is concentrated on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash low-latency paths, ROCm model enablement, attention/kernel optimization, and correctness fixes around prefix caching and KV connectors.

1. Today's Highlights

No new vLLM releases landed, but development activity remains high. Non-CUDA hardware paths are explicitly out of scope for this PR. Anyone pinning a 3.10 runtime for CUDA builds should plan a bump.

3. New Model & Hardware Support

  • SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, PCIe-only) — Field report for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8× RTX PRO 6000 with measured prefill/decode and a speculative-decoding A/B (#40877). A separate tracking issue covers required fixes for GLM-5.3-Flash on SM120 TP2 with W4A16 routed experts, FP8 KV, vision, and native MTP (#37813).
  • Hopper (SM90) KDA verify kernel — #44612 extends the fused CuTe DSL KDA (fused_kda_decode_mtp_dspark) verify kernel to SM90; previously gated to SM100+ due to paired FP32 instructions.
  • AMD / ROCm — AITER upgrade readiness tracker remains active (#21302); PR #44008 carries tuned DSv4 GEMM rows and mHC tile_m=16 until upstream AITER ships them. Diffusion multimodal unit tests are being made ROCm-aware (#44599).
  • Tokenizer backend RFC — toktier, an opt-in exact incremental and chunk-parallel CPU tokenizer backend (#44374).
  • Monokernel framework RFC — in-tree python/sglang/experimental/monokernels/ plugin model for per-model fused kernels (#43949).

4. Performance & Optimization

  • AMD MI355X, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8: fuse 1x128 activation quant (~4 µs) into the small-M block-scale GEMM (~9 µs) per dense FP8 projection — targeted at EAGLE low-concurrency decode (#42229).
  • AMD linear-attn: skip the unused PP-spec compare on the GDN/KDA verify path for Qwen3.5-397B (#43861).
  • NIXL KV packing for TP-heterogeneous transfer (Muse Spark Open) (#44615).
  • Unified memory pool: prewarm the compaction move at startup and copy whole page envelopes by page id, removing first-use kernel compile/load and _assert_async cost from the serving path (#44592).
  • Diffusion runtime import: defer full GC collections during ~10k-module import, avoiding repeated full heap traces (#44606).
  • Tool schema validation: replace pure-Python Draft202012Validator.check_schema (~0.7 ms/tool, ~12 ms for an 18-tool agent request on the API event loop) with jsonschema-rs (#43274).
  • CUDA graph: keep deepstack media prefills eager so Qwen3-VL-family graph replays don't reuse a stale input_deepstack_embeds (#44607).

5. Stability & Regressions

Ranked by severity; fix PRs noted where present.

  1. Silent KV corruption — PD prefill + HiCache (#44070): with the default SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_EARLY_SEND_CACHED_PREFIX=1, decode can receive stale KV for part of a prefix when two requests share a prefix whose KV is only in host memory. Silent wrong results, not a crash. No fix PR referenced.
  2. Whole-engine crash on client disconnect (#39216): uncaught asyncio.CancelledError bypasses except Exception; reproducible on 4× RTX 6000D / DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
  3. OOM crash of the entire TP group (#41076): unbounded SparsePrefillWorkspace allocation with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSPARK.
  4. Kimi K3 decode crash (#34920): PD disagg + --dcp-size 8 + DSPARK target-verify hits cumsum(extend_prefix_lens=None) in dcp/planner.py; all TP ranks die.
  5. GLM-5.3-Flash degenerate output with DFLASH speculative decoding (#40843): severe repetition/loops in reasoning output.
  6. GLM-5.3-Flash !-loop under agentic prompts (#36669): complex system prompt + multiple tools + tool_choice=auto degenerates thinking output.
  7. SM120 attention backend matrix (#42012): fa4 crashes at CUDA-graph capture on hybrid extend reshape; triton is the only working backend on the tested v0.5.20 image.
  8. NIXL PD abort hang (#44369): abort can leave all default transfer workers waiting on healthy non-terminal handles.
  9. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next silent semantic corruption (#37111): QSA + NEXTN decode graph on GB10 TP2.
  10. Synchronous request preprocessing blocks the event loop (#30770), delaying health endpoints — deterministic CPU-only repro.
  11. Unbounded multimodal audio decode (#43708).
  12. Minor/test-infra: WeightChecker.reset_tensors filling MRotaryEmbedding.axis_map with random values (#44501); profiler filename path-traversal via caller-controlled output_dir/profile_prefix (#44609, fix open).
  13. CI flakiness: tracker #42752; NIXL storage tests sharing fixed /tmp dirs (#44613, fix open); hicache prefetch timeout budget re-issued per retry (#44614, fix open).

Closed today: #34340 (SM103 mis-gated as SM100 family, cutedsl TGV BF16 GEMM / trtllm-gen MoE finalize), #36333 (zombie request from disconnected streaming client), #21065 (CI maintenance mode), #23494 (AMD Q2 roadmap, marked inactive), #41303 (DeepSeek-V4.1 SWA bounded-replay window), #44599 (ROCm-aware diffusion tests).

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Validate PD + prefix caching carefully. If you run disaggregated prefill with HiCache and shared system prompts (the normal agent case), #44070 means identical prefixes can yield subtly wrong outputs with no error surfaced. Consider SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_EARLY_SEND_CACHED_PREFIX=0 until fixed, and add output-quality canaries on shared-prefix traffic.
  • Harden against disconnect-driven failures. #39216 is an engine-wide crash on client abort, and #44369 can wedge transfer workers. Gateways should retry on connection errors, but expect some fraction of aborts to take a whole replica down — run N+1 capacity and automate restarts.
  • Agentic workloads have two independent hazards. GLM-5.3-Flash degenerates under multi-tool prompts (#36669) and under DFLASH speculative decoding (#40843); add repetition watchdogs or disable DFLASH for these routes. Separately, tool-schema validation costs ~0.7 ms per tool on the API event loop, so 10–20 tool agents pay 7–14 ms before generation starts (#43274 is the fix in review).
  • SM120 deployments are the least-battle-tested path. Multiple independent reports converge on the same guidance: triton is the reliable attention backend, fa4 breaks CUDA-graph capture, and GLM-5.3-Flash still needs a fix set before production (#42012, #37813, #40877).
  • Cheap wins are available if you're on AMD/MI355X — the FP8 quant+GEMM fusion (#42229) targets exactly the low-concurrency EAGLE decode regime that interactive agents run in.

4. Performance & Optimization

  • MLX engine is single-request serial — requests are processed strictly FIFO regardless of OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL, with no continuous batching. One issue closed (#17666), the feature request for batching/parallel decode remains open (#17280, 👍 4).

  • Tool-call opening tags lost across streaming chunk boundaries (DeepSeek3, Cogito, LFM2 parsers) — fix PR with 219 passing tests. (#19028)
  • gemma4 with think: false returns empty reply after a tool response — empty thought block never closed. (#18861)

Medium — pull/transfer and startup

  • ollama pull broken with SOCKS proxy since 0.40.4 (works on 0.34.4) — closed. (#19035)
  • Pull failures: redirect target not allowed / DNS resolution of R2 endpoint (#18716) and max retries exceeded (#18842).

Low — desktop / API edge cases

  • Desktop app memory leak — context-menu label C strings allocated and never freed. (#19029)

6. What This Means for Application Developers

  • Prefer /v1 over native /api/chat for tool-calling agents right now. The native route reportedly empties tool definitions, while the OpenAI-compatible route renders them correctly (#19040). Validate tool schemas end-to-end before shipping.
  • Beware silent numeric truncation in Go clients when round-tripping tool-call arguments — apply the pending fix or add your own lossless decoding (#18942).
